blocks.text: Thermal physics deals with the relationship between heat, work, temperature and other forms of energy. The laws of thermodynamics describe how energy changes in a system and how the system can do useful work on its surroundings.

A large system containing many atoms or molecules is called a macroscopic system, and a system of a single atom or molecule is a microscopic system. Macroscopic systems have properties such as temperature and pressure, which belong to the whole system and can be studied without referring to molecules. Microscopic systems have properties such as kinetic energy and momentum. Thermal physics deals with very large numbers of particles, of the order of Avogadro's number: atoms or molecules in gases, liquids and solids, and even electrons in metals and neutrons in neutron stars.

The kinetic theory of gases has many everyday applications, for example in car engines, turbines, pumps, air conditioners, food production and the environment. Thermal physics draws on both the kinetic theory of gases and statistical mechanics.

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between a macroscopic and a microscopic system? Give one property of each.
blocks.explanation: A macroscopic system contains very many atoms or molecules (property: temperature or pressure); a microscopic system is a single atom or molecule (property: kinetic energy or momentum).
